SCHEMA REQUEST to p2-deps-scaffold (owner of artifacts.py and runlog.py). The page a licence string was read from is recorded PER RUN, in the G0 stage's runlog `notes.licence_pages` ({source_id: url}), because artifacts.INGESTED_SENTENCE is `additionalProperties: false` with no `licence_page` property and runlog.LicenceRow has five fixed fields. Per-sentence recording needs either a `licence_page` property on INGESTED_SENTENCE or a sixth field on LicenceRow; both files are outside this lane. Until then no comment, docstring or report in this lane claims a per-sentence page — the three that did were corrected.
heldWithoutAnInvariantId: The licence gate is a CAPABILITY, not a check. `IngestPermit.__init__` demands a module-private token, so a permit can only come from `sources.licences.permit()`; every fetcher takes one; `licences.open_transport(permit, …)` is the only way to obtain something a fetcher can call `get`/`stream` on; and `require()` re-derives the verdict from config.SOURCES before EVERY request rather than once per run. An `is_allowed(source) -> bool` helper would satisfy the invariant's wording and be defeated by the next lane simply not calling it.

Redirects are followed BY THE GATE, not by httpx. `HttpTransport` sets `follow_redirects=False` and raises `Redirected(location)`; `GatedTransport` catches it, re-runs the host check and the licence check on the new URL, and only then makes the next hop (bounded by MAX_REDIRECT_HOPS). Before this, a 302 from a permitted host to an unclassified one was followed inside httpx under a permit granted for the first — the class docstring claimed otherwise and the code did not enforce it.

The OPUS reader is a RANGED reader, not a streaming one, and that is a correctness property rather than an optimisation: a moses archive holds one member per side and the second begins after the first ends, so sequential streaming of `en-es` (measured live 2026-09-12 at 40,327,884,789 bytes) would have to read 40 GB to reach the Spanish side. It reads the central directory from the tail (zip64 included — every archive worth capping is over 4 GB) and then the front of each member in 8 MB slices, stopping at --max-pairs. Peak memory is one slice.

The Tatoeba read is capped on ALL THREE files, not only the target side. The links file stops at `max_pairs`; the English side stops as soon as every linked English id has text (it is a lookup table, not a corpus, and reading past the last wanted id is 100+ MB of pure waste); the target side stops at `max_pairs`. Every one of the three also carries a compressed-byte ceiling (MAX_STREAM_BYTES_DEFAULT) so a pathological export cannot fill the build machine's disk.

Live re-verification on 2026-09-12 of the four facts this lane is built on, all confirmed to the byte: spa_sentences_CC0.tsv.bz2 = 2,266 bytes (R4); lowercase sentences_cc0.tar.bz2 -> 404 and uppercase sentences_CC0.tar.bz2 -> 200, 7,958,579 bytes (R3); en-de.txt.zip -> 404 and de-en.txt.zip -> 200, 21,180,847,796 bytes (the direction rule); the OPUS API's NLLB row for en-es reporting `size: 1` against a 40.3 GB archive (R2).

Two bugs the tests caught before the code left the lane: a STORED zip member with no length bound ran off the end of its own data and decoded the NEXT member's local file header as sentences; and an OPUS API 404 raised by the transport bypassed the branch that names the alphabetical pair rule, so the operator who typed `en-de` would have got a bare 404.

The register filter rejects markup, crawl artefacts, untranslated identical pairs and an explicitly short profanity list. Short on purpose: this is an A1 lesson-content filter, not a moderation system, and a long deny list quietly deletes ordinary vocabulary. G6 and the paid reviewer sample are the real quality gates.

Normalisation folds only what is invisible — NFC, zero-width joiners, BOMs, soft hyphens, repeated whitespace — and never diacritics. `año` is not `ano`: folding them would merge two lemmas and V1 would then pass over a ledger that means nothing.
